units.translation: In M is read ἄλευ ᾶ δα [avoid, O earth], with the letters αλευα written over an erasure and all the accents added by the hand of the διορθωτοῦ [corrector]. For the first hand had written ὦ [O] instead of â, which is preserved in most copies, in which is written ἄλευ' [avoid] with an apostrophe and ὦ δᾶ [O earth]. To this the διορθωτής [corrector] added a scholion whose first part is more worthy of the ancient Alexandrian grammarian himself: γρ. [that is, γράφεται or γραπτέον] ἀλευάδα [Aleuada] patronymically from ἀλεύας [Aleuas]. Or 'which one must guard against.' Some read thus: ἄλευ ὦ δᾶ [avoid, O earth]; ἄλευ [avoid], ἀναχώρει [withdraw], ἔκκλινε [turn aside]; and ὦ δᾶ [O earth], ὦ γῆ [O earth]. For the Dorians call the earth δῆν [earth] and δᾶν [earth], and darkness δνόφον [darkness]. The last of these are similar to what is read in Etym. M. p. 60,8: ἀλευάδα [Aleuada] is said like φεύδα [alas, earth] (that is φεῦ δᾶ [alas, earth]). For the Dorians call the earth δᾶν [earth], as also darkness δνόφον [darkness]. φεύδα [alas, earth] therefore is φεῦ γῆ [alas, earth]. Thus therefore also the (τὸ [the] omitted by cod. Voss. λευάδα [Aleuada]) ἀλέου δᾶ [avoid, earth] (δῆ [earth], with γῆ [earth] written above, codex Voss. δηλ cod. Dorvill.) with τοῦ δὲ [but the] standing for γῆ [earth], where in the lemma ἀλευάδα [Aleuada] alone by a scribal error is written for ἄλευ δᾶ [avoid, earth], or ἀλεύδα [avoid, earth], as φεύδα [alas, earth] is written for φεῦ δᾶ [alas, earth], but the last part, with the dittography removed, should be corrected thus: οὕτως οὖν καὶ ἄλευ δᾶ [thus therefore also avoid, earth] (or ἀλεύδα [avoid, earth]), with τοῦ δὲ [but the] standing for γῆ [earth]. For the comment about Aleuada is peculiar to the Aeschylean διορθωτοῦ [corrector] and foreign to the gloss of the Etymologicum, in whose words there is nothing that refers to the name Aleuada. From these things it appears that the ancient reading in Aeschylus was ἈΛΕΥΔΑ [ALEUDA], to which ὦ [O] before da was added by an interpreter, which the first hand of the Medicean codex preserved, with the meter violated. Therefore, having ejected ὦ [O], I have restored ἄλευ δᾶ [avoid, earth], although this is a singular apocope. For what Aristophanes Equit. 821 said παῦ παύε [stop, stop] and Aeschylus δίαιν δίαινε [moisten, moisten], which I restored Pers. 1038, where the codex has δίαινε δίαινε [moisten, moisten], is different, as I noted in Annot. Oxon. of the year 1841 on the verse of the Persians p. 318 with these words: "It is readily understood that this apocope has a place only where the same word is repeated. Therefore Aeschylus and Aristophanes could rightly say δίαιν διαίνε [moisten, moisten] and ποῦ παῦε [stop, stop], but they could not simply say δίαιν [moisten] and παῦ [stop]." Nor if Aeschylus said ἄλευ δᾶ [avoid, earth], whether first or following another, does it follow that he would ever have said ἄλευ [avoid] outside that formula.
